en.name: iMyCard
en.subtitle: Encrypted wallet on your phone
en.short_description: Cards, IDs and notes in an AES-256 vault, unlocked by face or finger.
en.description:
MyCard is a private wallet. Everything you put in it is encrypted on your device and unlocked with your face, fingerprint, or device passcode.

WHAT YOU CAN KEEP
37 card types across seven groups — payment and loyalty cards, ID documents and passports, travel and event passes, business cards, digital keys, notes, tasks and reminders. Add the fields that matter for each one; MyCard knows which are sensitive and masks them until you ask.

HOW IT IS PROTECTED
The vault is sealed with AES-256-GCM. GCM authenticates the whole file, so a tampered vault fails to open instead of silently decrypting to garbage. The key lives in the platform secure store, never in the vault file. "Erase all data" deletes every card and destroys the key — there is no copy anywhere else, so that is final.

STAYS ON YOUR DEVICE
There is no account, no cloud sync, and no server for your cards. Nothing you store ever leaves your phone, so nothing you store can be read by us. MyCard sends two things, and neither contains card data: a crash report if the app fails (the error and its stack trace, the device model, the app version and a random installation ID), and the requests for the ads described below. No analytics.

ADS
MyCard shows ads from Google AdMob in a banner below your card list; never on a card's details, the editor, the lock screen or Settings. Google may use device identifiers to serve and measure those ads. MyCard does not ask to track you across other companies' apps and websites, and where the law requires consent (for example in the EEA and the UK) ads are requested only after you have made a choice, which you can change at any time under Settings > Privacy choices.

ORGANISE IT
Tag cards, filter by group, archive what you are done with, and search the lot.

review_information.notes:
2. DEVICES AND OS VERSIONS TESTED
Automated tests run on every build: iPhone 17 Pro Max and iPad Pro 13-inch simulators on iOS 26, and a Pixel Android emulator on API 34.
Each release is also installed and launched on those targets, so a
build that cannot start never ships.

3. WHAT THIS APP DOES, AND FOR WHOM
MyCard is a private wallet. Everything you put in it is encrypted on your device and unlocked with your face, fingerprint, or device passcode.

Intended audience:
Encrypted wallet on your phone

4. SETTING UP AND REACHING THE MAIN FEATURES
No account and no login are required. Every feature is reachable from the first screen after launch.

5. EXTERNAL SERVICES USED
- Google AdMob (ads): a banner ad below the card list, requested through the Google Mobile Ads SDK behind Google UMP consent. Google may use device identifiers to serve and measure ads. The app does not request App Tracking Transparency (no IDFA) and does not read the Android advertising ID. Ad requests never contain card data.
- Firebase Crashlytics (Google): when the app crashes it sends a crash report: the error and stack trace, device model, OS and app version, and a random Crashlytics installation ID. No card data, no account and no user identifier are sent. Firebase Analytics and Performance Monitoring are linked through a shared library but deactivated and never started.
Everything the user stores stays on the device.

6. REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
The app follows the device language for 12 locales (Arabic, Chinese (Simplified), English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish), but translation is partial: shared labels are translated, while most screen text is in English only. Features are identical in every region.

7. REGULATED INDUSTRY OR THIRD-PARTY MATERIAL

The app is not in a regulated industry and carries no licensed third-party material. All content, artwork and copy are the developer's own.


ACCOUNT DELETION
The app creates no account, so there is nothing to delete.

differentiation:
1. WHAT IT DOES
MyCard is a private wallet. Everything you put in it is encrypted on your device and unlocked with your face, fingerprint, or device passcode.
Screens it contains: auth, cards, settings

2. INTENDED USER
People who want to keep their cards and documents — payment and loyalty cards, IDs and passports, travel passes, business cards, keys and notes — on their phone without giving them to a cloud service or creating an account. The vault is encrypted on the device and opened with face, fingerprint or passcode, and nothing stored leaves the phone. It suits users who prefer a wallet that cannot sync or be recovered from a server, accepting that erasing it is final.
